interactions.summary: Jiang opens by sketching the popular Knights Templar conspiracy template: a secret order survives as Freemasonry, engineers modern revolutions and wars, and culminates in a Jerusalem-centered one-world AI surveillance state animated by occult secrets and demon contracts.

He then dismantles that story as literal explanation: there is no evidence for demons or a thousand-year conspiracy, real elites do not believe it, and the theory is anti-historical and anti-game-theory. Yet he keeps it because it is intuitive, explanatory, and paradoxically predictive.
Jiang reframes the conspiracy story as a metaphor and begins his literal model: occultists seek the universe's hidden structure, starting with domains like astrology and alchemy.

claims.claim: Jiang presents the popular conspiracy story as a template in which the Knights Templars survive as Scottish Rite Freemasons and become the hidden driver of modern revolutions, wars, banking, and the coming AI surveillance state.
claims.temporal_scope: Lecture framing on 2026-05-19 of a conspiracy narrative Jiang is about to analyze.

claims.claim: A major variant of that conspiracy template says the hidden order gains occult power through demon contracts, ritual sacrifice, and secret knowledge that can yield immortality, advanced technology, and a one-world government that brings interdimensional beings into the world.
claims.temporal_scope: Lecture framing on 2026-05-19 of a speculative conspiracy variant.

claims.claim: Jiang rejects the conspiracy story as literal truth because there is no evidence for demons or for a thousand-year continuous plot, and because people with real power regard it as nonsense.

Jiang says the conspiracy template is anti-historical and anti-game-theory because it oversimplifies how power works and ignores the tendency of powerful actors to become arrogant, stupid, and vulnerable to collapse.
Even though the conspiracy theory is not factual, Jiang keeps it because it is intuitive, gives a clearer explanatory picture than school history, and remains predictive about the future.
claims.temporal_scope: Lecture claim on 2026-05-19 about the theory's interpretive usefulness.

claims.claim: Jiang's literal replacement model begins by distinguishing occultists or mystics, who seek the universe's hidden principles, from the conspiracy story's literal demonology; the earlier story is metaphorical, not literal.
claims.temporal_scope: Lecture pivot on 2026-05-19 into Jiang's own explanatory model.

signature_moments.moment: The theory is false as history but true as prediction: nonsense that still sees where the world is going.
signature_moments.source_phrase: this is not at all factual, but it is truthful
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is the packet's governing paradox and the hinge that lets Jiang move from conspiracy lore to his own model of power.

signature_moments.moment: Power does not stay perfectly coordinated; the iron law of history is that rulers become arrogant, stupid, and set themselves up for spectacular falls.
signature_moments.source_phrase: when people are in power, they become arrogant
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It marks Jiang's game-theoretic correction to totalizing conspiracy models.

signature_moments.moment: The occult story is kept as metaphor, then translated into a literal map of mystics trying to uncover the universe's hidden code.
signature_moments.source_phrase: this is metaphorical. It is not literal
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It preserves the lecture's core move from lurid myth to Jiang's explanatory architecture.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: Jiang's criticism that the conspiracy story ignores strategic friction, hubris, and the instability of power.
The predicted end-state in the conspiracy template: a one-world order using AI to monitor and govern human life.
People who try to uncover the hidden structure of the universe through domains like astrology, alchemy, and related esoteric study.

chronology_notes.note: On 2026-05-19 Jiang explicitly links this semester's game-theory frame to last semester's secret-history and eschatology material, then reclassifies the older conspiracy story as metaphor before offering a literal power model.
